2026-11-27 — Beta.6 B&W materials and film-selection recommendations

The existing 56 colour film and 12 colour print indices, profile bytes,
neutral filters, DIR defaults and 36 added-colour-film grain areas are retained.
Eight B&W films follow them: Kodak Double-X 5222; Kodak Tri-X Reversal 7266;
Ilford HP5 Plus, FP4 Plus and Delta 3200; Kodak T-Max 100; Fujifilm Acros II;
and experimental Kodak Tri-X 400 in D-76, 8 minutes at 20 C. Kodak 2302 and
experimental Ilford Multigrade RC Deluxe grade 2 follow the existing prints.
All ten source JSONs are copied from Negs 2f5b570 without numerical edits.
Their individual CC BY-SA 4.0 attribution, original sources and assumptions
remain embedded. Source records and preparation scripts for the two
experimental profiles are included in additional-stock-data.tar.gz;
manufacturer PDF/raster excerpts are excluded and retain their original rights.

B&W reference development times follow Negs' explicit normal-time field or
its floor-middle family entry: Double-X 6.5 min, Tri-X Reversal 1, HP5 6.5,
FP4 8, Delta 3200 9, T-Max 100 6, Acros II 7, Tri-X 400 8; 2302 5 and Ilford
grade 2 1. Tri-X Reversal's single family value is retained as source metadata;
it does not claim a one-minute complete real-world reversal process.
The runtime selects a single source time, retains all curve/grain components,
and maps the single silver-density channel to the native three-lane layout.
Inter-colour DIR terms are zero. The fourth grain component repeats the finest
source particle scale, as in Negs. No colour model or measured layer is invented.

Both B&W print materials accept B&W negatives only. Ilford grade 2 requires
normalized exposure and no preflash; its sensitivity is a neutral integration
weight, with no claim of calibrated colour-negative printing, absolute paper
speed, spectral filtration, variable contrast, paper tint or texture. Source
Tri-X 400 assumptions include an unmeasured shoulder and sensitivity-tail
truncation beyond 665 nm. Both experimental labels remain visible.

New stock_defaults.json describes all 64 film recommendations and 14 print
compatibility sets, including provenance. Negative-film target prints follow
the source profile; Double-X is paired with the available B&W cine print 2302
as a RAW Photo Editor recommendation. Reversal film bypasses printing. The
original 20 DIR recommendations match their bundled 0.3.2 profiles; later
stocks retain their matching source DIR. Grain areas are computed from the
reference-time source layer curves and source RMS granularity. Verita 200D
has no stock-specific RMS preset and explicitly uses the upstream generic
schema defaults. Grain/halation physical values are prepared with effects
disabled initially. These recommendations apply when a film is selected;
legacy saved recipe fallback remains separate.

Reproduce the source archive with pack_stock_data.py, then regenerate grain
areas and the recommendation JSON with pack_stock_grain.py. Data-integrity
checks compared every prior archive member and calibration entry, all prior
indices and all 36 prior grain-area triples without differences. GPU pixel
and installed-package acceptance are recorded separately for the release.

2026-11-27 — Additional profiles compiled into RAW Photo Editor

Additional film and print data are licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0
(https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/). Copyright for each
individual profile and its source measurements is documented inside that
profile. Film and print names identify the materials being simulated.

Source: Negs by Noah Haasis, revision 2f5b5703d807e9490801d9155ac30b2c19460551
https://github.com/noahhaasis/negs/tree/2f5b5703d807e9490801d9155ac30b2c19460551/data
Includes profiles from spektrafilm by Andrea Volpato
(https://github.com/andreavolpato/spektrafilm) and from Fotufilm by
MUAStudio Inc. (https://fotufilm.com, https://github.com/DhaliwalX/fotufilm-engine).
The applicable SPEKTRAFILM_LICENSE.txt, FOTUFILM_LICENSE.txt and upstream
CHANGELOG.txt are included under Legal/Negs in additional-stock-data.tar.gz.

RAW Photo Editor selected additional three-channel profiles with a complete
TH-KG3 neutral print-filter table. Profiles marked approximate by the source
were excluded. The supplied JSON retains the source values and per-stock
metadata. Additional paper targets include the Fujifilm Eterna-CP 3513DI,
3514DI, 3521XD and 3523XD motion-picture print films.

We compiled the measurements using the bundled Metal/Vulkan table generator.
The additional profiles' names follow the existing film and paper indices.
For these profiles we extracted the corresponding neutral filters and DIR
coupler coefficients from Negs. stock_grain.toml contains the source grain
presets with upstream notices. Lite uses the physical parameters supported
by its own grain model. The implementation and stock-specific responses
can differ from other applications using these materials.

Four additional profiles are from The Dyeworks 2.2.3 by Celian Le Bolloch,
https://github.com/natcelian/spektrafilm.exe/releases/tag/2.2.3. See the
included upstream notices in Legal/Dyeworks. Kodak Vision2 50D (5201),
100T (5212), and 500T (5260) were prepared from Kodak motion-picture
datasheets using Andrea Volpato's published profile factory. These retain
their source profiles' Vision3-derived adaptation parameters. The UltraMax
800 profile fits Kodak's E-7024 characteristic curves using the spectral
data from the related UltraMax 400 profile. All profiles and their
modifications are CC BY-SA 4.0. Their JSON metadata distinguishes the
datasheet values from inherited or estimated parameters.

For these four films on the eight existing print stocks, the enlarger settings
are from Dyeworks. For their 16 combinations with the four new Eterna-CP
print stocks, RAW Photo Editor derived TH-KG3 settings with Andrea Volpato's
solve_neutral_filter_shifts at spektrafilm commit 28bf883. The reference
pipeline exposes an 18.4% neutral patch and solves M and Y with C held at
zero. On the 16 resulting settings, the maximum relative R/G or B/G
deviation was below 0.000002 in that reference pipeline. The data are in
dyeworks-eterna-print-filters.json, CC BY-SA 4.0. Lite uses its own rendering
pipeline. See the included JSON for the individual filters and measurements.
